title: Adaptive Admission Gatekeeper for Incremental Model Launches
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a general-purpose admission gatekeeper that codifies step schedules, traffic-split semantics, and domain-specific guardrails for incremental model launches (canary, A/B, shadow). This ticket scopes the config DSL, evaluation hooks, rollback heuristics, and runtime enforcement model. Goals: 1) let product teams declare multi-step ramps and cohort slices with percent and time-based transitions; 2) provide deterministic, auditable automatic rollback triggered by user-configurable metric contracts; 3) support transparent shadow probing and traffic mirroring without impacting production paths; 4) emit structured telemetry and per-step annotations for the Console and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: Config DSL defined and documented (examples for canary, A/B, shadow) and validated by PM/Design
Runtime accepts admission config and enforces step transitions deterministically (no silent skips)
Automatic rollback triggers on at least three supported signals: 5xx rate increase, latency P95 breach, and semantic quality regression from eval hook
Shadow flows supported with sampled mirroring and isolated resource accounting (no user-visible traffic impact)
Integration tests covering step ramps, manual pause/resume, forced rollback, and overlapping concurrent rollouts
Console shows per-step traffic, telemetry, and a single-click abort that triggers rollback and annotates audit logs
implementation_notes: Design a compact DSL (YAML/JSON) with top-level fields: stages[], metrics[], abort_policy, shadow_config, cohorts[] — provide examples in docs
Prefer policy evaluation at the API gateway layer to short-circuit routing decisions; fall back to runtime agent when gateway feature flag disabled
Support both time-based and event-based step progression: e.g., step: {percent: 10, duration: 2h} and step: {percent: 30, until: metric('error_rate') < 0.02}
Rollback heuristics: require sustained breach over a sliding window (configurable), and cooldown period before re-admit attempts
For A/B experiments, allow parallel branches with independent metrics and a comparator block to declare winning criteria
KV cache and batching interactions: ensure intercepting gate does not flush per-request KV cache unexpectedly; run performance microbenchmarks
Security: audit every traffic-split action and store immutable snapshot of active config in control-plane datastore for post-mortem
Operational: emit 'step_start' and 'step_end' traces, include build_id, cohort_id, and sample request_ids for failing requests to tie to evaluations
updates: 2026-03-01 - Created: initial draft of objectives and acceptance criteria; scoped core checkpoints with PM and Design.

2026-03-03 - Arch sync: decided to implement policy evaluation in two places (gateway fast-path + runtime agent) to allow progressive rollout of enforcement. Ticket split created for gateway adapter (ENG-24790).
2026-03-05 - Design review: UX requested explicit 'safety hold' step type and clearer audit messages. Added 'hold' semantics to DSL draft and updated acceptance criteria.

2026-03-07 - Engineering spike: implemented prototype of time-windowed rollback signal evaluator; microbenchmarks show ~0.4ms added median latency at gateway path with caching enabled. Need further perf optimization for p99.
2026-03-09 - Security review kickoff: SSO and KMS gating for rollout config changes required. Raised follow-up for ACL enforcement (ENG-24800).

2026-03-10 - In-progress: wiring shadow mirroring into runtime's metric namespace; found race with sampler state when multiple rollouts share cohorts — added mitigation to implementation_notes and scheduled follow-up sub-issue ENG-24795.
notes_for_reviewers: Please review DSL examples in Confluence. We're trying to balance expressivity and simplicity — avoid introducing Turing-complete predicates unless strictly necessary.
Pay attention to the proposed default rollback thresholds. We're conservative by default (requires 3-sigma sustained breach) but allow project overrides.
Performance trade-offs: gateway enforcement is fast but requires protobuf/SDK changes; runtime enforcement is slower but safer for private deployments. Feedback welcome.
